candidates.title: Default-on flag makes every non-macOS take report 'Experimental native capture'
candidates.body: The flag is read with `isFlagEnabled(flag, FLAG_DEFAULTS[flag])` (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:422-424) and sent to main as `requested`. Main computes `experimentalRequested = requestedByFlag || --experimental-native-recording` before it checks the platform (apps/kaipu-record/src/main/recording/native/ipc.ts:50-61), so off macOS it returns `transportAvailable: false` with `experimentalRequested: true`. The renderer then calls `onNativeDecision('Experimental native capture: using Chromium. ...')` (recorder-engine.ts:430-433). The preload exposes `nativeCapture` on every platform (apps/kaipu-record/src/preload/index.ts:93), so the bridge is present on Windows and Linux. Before this change the default was false and those takes never reached the message. Now every Windows or Linux dev take shows a 10 s toast, and packaged builds log the line. Suggested fix: do not count the flag as a request off darwin (check the platform before the flag is passed, or skip the decision message when the transport is unavailable on that platform), and keep the default.

candidates.title: Packaged builds no longer show why a take fell back to Chromium
candidates.body: Before this change every build toasted the native decision. Now only dev builds toast it, and a packaged build only runs `console.info` (recorder-store.ts:523-524). The fallback reasons include: the watermark (recorder-engine.ts:1416), a helper that is missing or incompatible (ipc.ts:70-76), a cursor track that is unavailable (recorder-engine.ts:434-439), and a failed helper preparation (recorder-engine.ts:467-471). The console is not collected: analytics-client.ts:54-68 only sends exceptions and named events. So a packaged user who expected an editable cursor sees only that the editor offers no Cursor entry, with no reason, and the failure does not reach PostHog. The comment says the decision is a developer diagnostic, which is a deliberate choice, but the helper-preparation and helper-missing failures are errors. Question for the author: should those reach `captureEvent` (or `captureException`) in packaged builds, or keep the toast for them?

candidates.title: Kill switch does not reach users with diagnostics off or no flag response
candidates.body: Lines 69-70 say a 0% rollout makes every build read `false` and the next take uses Chromium. In code, `isFlagEnabled` returns the default whenever PostHog has not started, which is when diagnostics are off (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/analytics/analytics-client.ts:77), and whenever `isFeatureEnabled` is undefined, which covers offline use and flags that have not loaded yet (analytics-client.ts:78-79). With the default now `true` (apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/analytics.ts:26), those users run native capture and cannot be switched off remotely. Before this change the default was false, so they were on Chromium. The section should state this scope. The SDK claim that posthog-js returns `undefined` for a disabled flag could not be checked here: node_modules is absent and the lockfile pins posthog-js 1.395.0 (bun.lock:2967).

candidates.title: Flag docs say 'Frame' and omit the watermark exception
candidates.body: The table row (and analytics.ts:23-24) says native capture is 'for Screen, Frame and Window' and does not mention that watermark takes never go native. The engine refuses them (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/recording/recorder-engine.ts:1411-1418, 'watermark requires Chromium'), and the backlog banner says so (backlog/cursor-sprite-capture.md:13). 'Frame' is the library label for area recordings (apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/recording-capture.ts:145-164, `captureFrame`). The code's mode is `area` (recording-capture.ts:44-50). Use the code's name and state the watermark exception. The watermark is a user setting (apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/watermark/use-watermark.ts:22-23), so the share of takes that go native depends on the user.

candidates.title: Is the owner gate in ADR 0047 met before the flag goes on by default?
candidates.body: ADR 0047 (Proposed, not Accepted) says the owner's gate for turning the flag on is that area and window sources work under native with the webcam, mic and system audio on (apps/documentation/src/content/docs/architecture/decisions/0047-native-capture-crops-at-the-source-streams-window-geometry-and-drops-the-bubble-fallback.mdx:21-23). Its Non-goals list 'Turning the flag on' and 'a signed helper' (lines 117-118). This banner turns the flag on and says the first signed release is still pending. ADR 0037 line 104 rejects native-first as the default, but 0037 is also Proposed, so this is not a breach of an accepted ADR. Please confirm the gate was met, or update the ADRs' status and context (0047 line 21 still reads 'flag (off)') in this change.

candidates.title: Stale 'experiments stay off' comment and misleading test name
candidates.body: The FLAG_DEFAULTS comment says experiments stay off (line 19). That is no longer true for `native-cursor-capture`, which now defaults to on. The test at apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/analytics.test.ts:14 is still named 'defaults every known flag to a safe value' and now pins a default that turns a capture path on. Reword both.

candidates.title: Frontmatter description still describes a deferred feature
candidates.body: The description reads 'Future improvement ... Deferred from v2; reopen if zoomed cursors look bad in production'. That contradicts the green status banner, which says native capture is on by default. The description is what index and sidebar readers see. Update it to match the status.
